meta.changelog: v3.0.0 (May 26 2026): Updated all program statuses to reflect today's date; added 7 new programs (Stanford AI4ALL, CMU AI Scholars, Princeton AI4ALL, NYU Tandon ARISE, Wharton Global Youth, Babson Summer Study, Columbia ENG); added 6 new events (Congressional App Challenge, HMMT, IOAI, Science Olympiad, LexHack, Hack Club Scrapyard).

programs.name: Research Science Institute (RSI)
programs.host: MIT / Center for Excellence in Education
programs.desc: The most prestigious STEM summer program in the US. 100 rising seniors conduct original research mentored by MIT scientists in labs across Boston. ~3,000 applicants, ~100 admitted (~3%). Covers the full research cycle: coursework, lab work, and a formal conference-style presentation. Fully free — tuition, housing, meals all covered.
programs.note: Applications for 2026 closed Dec 10, 2025. Applications for RSI 2027 typically open in October 2026 at cee.org.

programs.name: MITES Summer
programs.desc: Rigorous 6-week residential program for rising seniors passionate about STEM. Acceptance rate 1.5–4% — among the most selective HS programs in the US. Five college-level courses in math, life sciences, physics, engineering, and a project elective. Prioritizes underrepresented students but all US citizens/permanent residents may apply. All costs covered.
programs.note: Applications for 2026 closed Feb 2. Apply in fall of junior year for 2027 — same application as MITES Semester.

programs.name: PROMYS
programs.desc: One of the most prestigious math programs in the world. ~75 students spend 6 weeks exploring deep number theory and proof-based mathematics as practicing mathematicians. Application requires solving a rigorous problem set. Must have completed 9th grade and be at least 14. Free for families earning under $80k.
programs.note: 2026 application is closed. Applications for PROMYS 2027 open in January 2027 at promys.org.

programs.name: HCSSiM
programs.desc: A legendary 6-week math summer program in its 54th year. ~51 students explore college-level mathematics with unparalleled faculty access. 4-hour morning classes Mon–Sat plus evening problem sessions. Application includes the 'Very Interesting Test'. Rolling decisions — closed when full. Free for families under $85k.
programs.note: Applications for 2026 are closed. Apply for 2027 at hcssim.org — typically opens in January.

programs.name: MathROOTS
programs.desc: A free 2-week residential math accelerator at MIT for high-potential students from underrepresented backgrounds. Rigorous combinatorics, number theory, and geometry at a college level. Nationally selective; housing and meals fully covered. Strongly encourages Black, Hispanic, and Indigenous applicants.
programs.note: 2026 deadline was March 3. Open to students completing 9th or 10th grade. Apply for 2027 in early spring.

programs.name: TASS (Telluride Summer Seminar)
programs.desc: One of the most selective humanities programs in the US. ~30 students per program attend 5-week college-level seminars in Critical Black Studies (CBS) or Anti-Oppressive Studies (AOS). Tuition, books, room, board, field trips, and travel all covered. Open to sophomores and juniors (ages 15–17). Acceptance rate ~3–5%.
programs.note: 2026 deadline was December 3, 2025. Applications for TASS 2027 open in October 2026.

programs.name: Simons Summer Research Program
programs.desc: Rising seniors conduct hands-on research with Stony Brook faculty in science, math, or engineering. Must be nominated by school (max 2 per school). Acceptance rate below 5%. Concludes with a research poster and stipend award. No tuition charged. US citizens and permanent residents only.
programs.note: Closed. Requires school nomination. Stipend provided at conclusion. Apply in January of junior year for 2027.

programs.name: Summer Science Program (SSP)
programs.desc: One of the oldest and most prestigious STEM programs in the US (since 1959). Rising seniors spend 5 weeks doing authentic research in Astrophysics, Biochemistry, Bacterial Genomics, or Cell Biology. Teams of 3, ~700 total spots. Need-blind admissions with generous financial aid — many attend free. Alumni network of 4,300+ scientists and engineers.
programs.note: 2026 domestic deadline was Feb 19. Need-blind admissions means cost is based on family income. Apply in junior year for 2027. SSP is comparable in prestige to RSI and MITES.

programs.name: Broad Summer Scholars Program (BSSP)
programs.desc: Rising seniors from the Greater Boston area conduct cutting-edge research at the Broad Institute (affiliated with MIT and Harvard). Research areas: cancer biology, psychiatric disease, computational genomics, infectious disease, and more. Free plus a $3,600 stipend. No prior research experience required. ~20–30 students selected.
programs.note: 2026 deadline was January 21. Limited to students attending high school in the Greater Boston area. Free with a $3,600 stipend.

programs.name: NASA SEES Internship
programs.host: NASA / UT Austin Center for Space Research
programs.desc: Sophomores and juniors (must be 16 by July 5) analyze real NASA satellite data alongside NASA scientists. Includes a 2-week residential stay at UT Austin with housing and meals. Virtual science symposium July 20–21. ~215 students selected from ~2,000 applicants (~10%). US citizens only.
programs.note: 2026 deadline closed Feb 22. Must be in 10th or 11th grade. $2,000 cost — scholarship available for financial need.

programs.name: MIT Beaver Works Summer Institute
programs.desc: Rising seniors complete free online prerequisite courses, then apply for the 4-week summer session. 14+ tracks including autonomous vehicles, quantum computing, cybersecurity, satellite design, ML, and hardware hacking. Free for families earning under $90k; up to $2,350 for higher incomes. No housing provided.
programs.note: 2026 applications are now closed (April 20 deadline passed). Check bwsi.mit.edu in late 2026 for 2027 cycle.

programs.name: Carnegie Mellon SAMS
programs.desc: 6-week residential program at CMU for rising seniors from underrepresented backgrounds. Full scholarship: tuition, housing, meals, and a stipend. Prioritizes first-generation college students and students from underserved communities.
programs.note: Deadline passed. Open to US citizens/permanent residents from underrepresented backgrounds. Fully funded.

programs.name: COSMOS — CA Summer School for Math & Science
programs.loc: UC Davis, UC San Diego, UC Irvine, UC Santa Cruz
programs.desc: 4-week residential program for students passionate about STEM. 12+ cluster tracks per campus including AI/ML, astrophysics, bioengineering, marine science, robotics, and math. Led by UC faculty. Priority to California residents, but nationally open.
programs.note: 2026 applications closed Feb 6. Apply in January of 9th–11th grade for 2027.

programs.name: UIUC Young Scholars Program
programs.desc: 6-week research experience for rising 10th–12th graders with UIUC faculty mentors. Research areas include AI, cancer immunology, quantum mechanics, materials science, and neuroscience. Housing, meals, and a monetary award provided. Priority to students from IL, IN, KY, MI, MO, IA, WI.
programs.note: Deadline closed. Midwest priority but all US students eligible. Apply in February of sophomore or junior year.

programs.name: MITES Semester (Online)
programs.desc: Free 6-month online STEM program for rising seniors, designed as an alternative to MITES Summer. Rigorous online courses, virtual workshops, and college admissions counseling. Same application as MITES Summer — you are offered one or the other, not both.
programs.note: Same application and deadline as MITES Summer (Feb 2). If admitted, you receive a single offer — Summer or Semester.

programs.name: Yale Young Global Scholars (YYGS)
programs.desc: Academically intensive 2-week program in 8 interdisciplinary tracks including Applied Science, Biological Science, Frontiers of Medicine, International Affairs & Security, Law & Politics, and Sustainability. 1,600+ students from 120+ countries per year. Strong need-based aid.
programs.note: 2026 deadline was January 7. Need-based aid covers full cost for qualifying families. Apply in fall/early winter for 2027.

programs.name: Economics for Leaders (EFL)
programs.desc: Competitive week-long program at universities nationwide. Future leaders study how economic analysis applies to real policy decisions. ~2 applicants accepted per school. Fully funded: tuition, room, and board. Nominations often come through economics or social studies teachers.
programs.note: Deadline passed. Ask your economics or social studies teacher about nominations for 2027.

programs.name: Bank of America Student Leaders
programs.desc: Paid 8-week internship at a local nonprofit at ~$18/hr plus a week-long leadership summit in Washington, DC. One of the few fully paid internship programs open to high schoolers. Develops community leadership skills and nonprofit sector experience.
programs.note: 2026 deadline was March 9. Check your local Bank of America branch website for city-specific 2027 deadlines.

programs.name: Duke Pre-College Summer Programs
programs.desc: 1–3 week intensive on-campus sessions taught by Duke faculty. All 2026 programs are in-person only. Topics include neuroscience, AI, marine biology, engineering design, and global health. Must be at least 16 by June 29, 2026. 3.0+ GPA required.
programs.note: Application deadline has passed for 2026. Check precollege.duke.edu in early 2027 for the next cycle. Must be 16+ by June 29.

programs.name: UCSB Early Research Scholars Program
programs.desc: Students earn 4 UC transferable college credits through rigorous research at UCSB. 12+ tracks including neuroscience, CS, marine biology, physics, and chemistry. 3.5+ GPA recommended. Students write a formal research paper and present at a closing symposium.
programs.note: Deadline passed. Partial aid available for CA residents.

programs.name: Stanford Summer Humanities Institute
programs.desc: A 3-week residential program where students engage with big questions in humanities, social science, and law at Stanford. Daily seminars led by Stanford faculty. Selective; strong need-based financial aid program.
programs.note: Deadline passed. Strong financial aid available. Separate from Stanford Pre-Collegiate Studies.

programs.name: JHU Center for Talented Youth (CTY)
programs.desc: Wide range of intensive academic courses for academically talented students. Residential programs at JHU and partner colleges, plus online sessions. Courses span STEM, writing, humanities, and research. Designed for advanced learners. Multiple financial aid options available.
programs.note: Most 2026 sessions are now full as of late May. Check cty.jhu.edu for any remaining availability or register for 2027 notification.

programs.name: Harvard Pre-College Program
programs.desc: Two-week residential program where rising juniors and seniors (must be 16–18) take Harvard courses without the pressure of grades. Three sessions offered. $6,100 covers tuition, room, meals, and insurance. Limited need-based scholarships. Must graduate in 2027 or 2028.
programs.note: Applications for 2026 are now closed. Check summer.harvard.edu in January 2027. Must be at least 16 by June 20, 2026.

programs.name: Cornell Summer College
programs.desc: Take actual Cornell undergraduate courses for 3–8 weeks and earn transferable college credit. Programs in engineering, architecture, business, law, life sciences, and liberal arts. Full campus experience on Cornell's scenic Ithaca campus.
programs.note: Still accepting! Rolling admissions. Limited financial aid. Credit transferable to most US colleges.

programs.name: Georgetown Pre-College Programs
programs.desc: Summer programs in government, international affairs, pre-law, business, and STEM on Georgetown's historic campus in Washington, DC. DC location adds unique access to policy briefings, government agencies, and international organizations.
programs.note: 2026 deadline (April 15) has passed. Apply for 2027 in early spring. DC location is especially valuable for students interested in policy, law, or government.

programs.name: Davidson Academy Online
programs.desc: Free online accredited school and summer enrichment for profoundly gifted students (top 99.9th percentile). Summer courses go far beyond typical high school curricula. Students engage in college-level coursework with expert instructors and a global community of intellectual peers.
programs.note: Requires IQ documentation at the 99.9th percentile or above. Rolling applications year-round. For profoundly gifted students only.

programs.name: Rice University STEM Programs
programs.desc: Multiple programs including STEM@Rice, research apprenticeships, and the BYTE! coding academy. Topics span biomedical hardware, robotics, AI, and engineering. Some programs are competitive and free with stipends; others have moderate tuition.
programs.note: 2026 application window (April) has closed. Check Rice OCED in spring 2027 for the next cycle.

programs.name: Cold Email Research Apprenticeships
programs.dl: Reach out now — late but possible
programs.desc: Email professors directly at nearby universities to request summer research apprenticeships. Write a concise, genuine cold email with your resume, transcript, and specific interest in the lab's work. Personalization dramatically improves acceptance rates. Many PIs still finalizing summer rosters in late May/early June.
programs.note: Still worth trying in late May/early June — some PIs are still finalizing rosters. Email 15–20 labs to maximize chances. Include a tailored paragraph about their specific research.

programs.name: Canada/USA Mathcamp
programs.cost: ~$5,500 (generous need-based aid; free for low-income families)
programs.desc: One of the world's most prestigious math summer programs. ~120 students ages 13–18 from around the globe spend 6 weeks in deep, self-directed mathematical exploration. Students choose their own courses from a vast menu of advanced topics — everything from combinatorics and algebraic geometry to mathematical physics. The Qualifying Quiz (a challenging take-home problem set) is the centerpiece of the application. Vibrant community of math-loving peers. Generous financial aid — many students attend free.
programs.note: 2026 deadline was February 23. Location rotates each year; 2026 is at Champlain College in Burlington, VT. Apply for 2027 in January at mathcamp.org.

programs.name: Stanford SIMR
programs.loc: Stanford, CA (commuter only — Bay Area preference)
programs.cost: Free ($50 application fee, waivable for families under $80k)
programs.desc: One of the most prestigious biomedical research internships in the US. ~50 rising juniors and seniors perform original research with Stanford faculty across 8 institutes: cancer biology, stem cell research, immunology, neuroscience, bioengineering, genomics, cardiovascular science, and computational biology. 8-week program with a closing research symposium. Commuter only — students must live in the Bay Area.
programs.note: 2026 deadline was February 21. Strong preference for Bay Area residents (commuter program). Apply for 2027 in December.

programs.name: Clark Scholars Program
programs.desc: One of the smallest and most competitive research programs in the US — only ~12 students admitted nationally each year (~5% acceptance rate). Students work one-on-one with Texas Tech faculty for 7 weeks on original research in biology, chemistry, CS, physics, engineering, or history. Free: tuition, housing, meals, and weekend activities all covered, plus a $750 stipend. Must be at least 17 and a US citizen or permanent resident.
programs.note: 2026 deadline was February 16. Only 12 students admitted — among the most selective research experiences available to high schoolers. Apply January 2027.

programs.name: Garcia Scholars Program
programs.desc: Intensive 7-week research program in polymer science and materials science at Stony Brook University. Students conduct original laboratory research under faculty mentors and present results at a formal symposium. Strong record of student publications and competition placements. Must be at least 16 by July 4, 2026.
programs.note: 2026 applications are closed. Check stonybrook.edu/garcia in January 2027 for the next cycle.

programs.name: SUMaC (Stanford University Mathematics Camp)
programs.dates: Residential: Jun 21–Jul 17 · Online Session 1: Jun 15–Jul 3 · Online Session 2: Jul 6–Jul 24, 2026
programs.desc: One of the most prestigious math summer programs in the US, now in its 30th year. Rising 10th and 11th graders explore proof-based abstract algebra, number theory, or algebraic topology. Admission requires completing a challenging take-home exam (the SUMaC Admission Exam). Residential program (40 students) and two online sessions (64 students total). Daily problem sets and a heavy mathematical workload modeled on undergraduate courses.
programs.note: 2026 applications are closed. Apply for 2027 at sumac.spcs.stanford.edu — applications typically open in November with a February deadline.

programs.name: Google CSSI
programs.cost: Free (stipend provided to cover equipment/internet costs)
programs.desc: Google's Computer Science Summer Institute is a free 4-week online CS program for graduating high school seniors (rising college first-years) — especially students from groups historically underrepresented in tech. Students learn programming fundamentals, work on collaborative projects, attend workshops with Google engineers, and build their professional network. A stipend covers technology and connectivity costs.
programs.note: For graduating seniors (class of 2026) only — not for current 9th–11th graders. Applications typically open in January with a February–March deadline. Check g.co/cssi each January for the current cycle.

programs.name: Girls Who Code Pathways Program (Virtual)
programs.desc: Computer science & coding tracks (Data Science, Game Design, Web Development, AI/Society). 7-week online program open to all genders. Emphasis on social impact applications of technology.
programs.note: 2026 deadline was April 10. Free program. Accepts international students.

programs.name: Princeton University Laboratory Learning Program
programs.desc: Research internship in natural sciences & engineering at Princeton. Commuter program — students must provide own transportation.
programs.note: 2026 deadline passed. Free program (no tuition). US citizens and permanent residents only. Commuter-only.

programs.name: Lumos Fellows
programs.desc: Computer science & AI online program. 6-week virtual program with financial aid and merit scholarships available.
programs.note: 2026 spring session is closed. Check lumosfellows.com for future cohorts.

programs.name: Institute for Mathematics and Democracy – HS Summer Research
programs.desc: Mathematics, democracy & data analysis. Free 6-week virtual program exploring the intersection of math and democratic systems.
programs.note: 2026 deadline was March 6. Free program. Accepts international students.

programs.name: Engineering Summer Program (ESP) – UW-Madison
programs.desc: Engineering & STEM residential program at UW-Madison. Free 3-week residential experience for underrepresented students interested in engineering.
programs.note: 2026 deadline was March 9. Free program. US citizens only (no international).

programs.name: Fred Hutch Summer High School Internship (SHIP)
programs.desc: Biomedical research & lab techniques paid internship at the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center in Seattle. In-person 8-week program.
programs.note: 2026 deadline was March 13. Paid internship. US citizens only.

programs.name: Seattle Children's Research Training Program
programs.desc: Biomedical research & public health commuter program at Seattle Children's. Free 4-week program with a $2,000 stipend for participants.
programs.note: 2026 deadline was March 29. Free with $2,000 stipend. US citizens only.

programs.name: Scripps Research HS Student Research Education Program
programs.desc: Biomedical research & laboratory skills internship at Scripps Research in La Jolla, CA. Free paid program with pre-internship training followed by a 7-week lab internship.
programs.note: 2026 deadline was March 22. Paid internship. US citizens only.

programs.name: Wistar Institute High School Biomedical Research Program
programs.dates: 4 weeks (option to extend to 7 weeks); Jul 6 2026
programs.desc: Biomedical research commuter internship at the Wistar Institute in Philadelphia. Free 4-week program (extendable to 7 weeks) with a $1,500 stipend.
programs.note: 2026 deadline was March 20. Free with $1,500 stipend. US citizens only.

programs.name: UCSF AI4ALL Biomedical Data Science Internship

programs.name: Institute for Systems Biology – Systems Education Experiences

programs.name: The Lundquist Institute – STAR Program

programs.name: Stanford AI4ALL
programs.desc: Stanford's premier AI access program for rising 10th graders. Hosted jointly by Stanford HAI and Stanford Pre-Collegiate Studies, AI4ALL introduces 9th-grade students to artificial intelligence through lectures, live demos with AI companies, team research projects, and career workshops. Tracks explore medical AI, computer vision, natural language processing, climate modeling, and robotics. Students present an original team project at a final symposium. Priority given to students from underrepresented communities. Both online (Jun 15–26) and residential (Jul 19–31) formats available. Completely free.
programs.note: 2026 deadline was February 6. Application is now closed. Open ONLY to current 9th graders. Apply for 2027 at ai4all.spcs.stanford.edu — applications typically open in December. Free for all admitted students.

programs.name: Carnegie Mellon AI Scholars
programs.desc: Fully funded 4-week residential AI program for rising high school seniors at CMU. Students take college-level classes in neural networks, NLP, and computer vision alongside seminars and group-based work. No prior AI or Python experience required — a pre-program Python course is provided one month before arrival. Teams develop a capstone research project addressing a real-world problem, presented at a final symposium. Students also attend college admissions workshops and student life sessions. Acceptance rate estimated under 5%.
programs.note: 2026 deadline was February 1. Only for rising seniors (at least 16). Must be a US citizen or permanent resident. Fully funded — tuition, housing, and meals covered. Apply for 2027 in January at cmu.edu.

programs.name: Princeton AI4ALL
programs.desc: A free 3-week residential AI program at Princeton University emphasizing 'AI for Social Good.' Rising 11th graders study the technical foundations of AI while exploring its ethical implications — bias, safety, and governance. Students participate in Princeton faculty lectures, a practical research project with mentorship from Princeton undergrads and grad students, and policy-focused field experiences. Program combines equal weight on technical and social dimensions of AI. Priority given to students from low-income backgrounds and underrepresented groups. Approximately 30 students selected nationally.
programs.note: 2026 deadline was February 15. Open to rising 11th graders from the US. Priority to low-income and underrepresented students. Fully free — tuition, housing, and meals covered. Apply for 2027 in January.

programs.name: NYU Tandon ARISE
programs.desc: Competitive 10-week STEM research internship at NYU's Tandon School of Engineering for NYC high school students in 10th or 11th grade. Students are matched with faculty mentors and work in research labs on projects in CS, robotics, AI, bioengineering, and data science. 76–80 spots available. Includes group seminars, lab tours, and college application workshops. Students receive a $2,000 stipend upon completion. Commuter program — no housing provided. Strong academic record and demonstrated STEM interest required. Students submit transcripts, an essay, and a letter of support.
programs.note: 2026 deadline was February 27. NYC high school students only (10th or 11th grade). Free + $2,000 stipend upon completion. Commuter program — no housing. Apply for 2027 at engineering.nyu.edu/arise.

programs.name: Wharton Global Youth Program
programs.desc: The leading high school business program in the US, offered by Wharton — the #1 undergraduate business school. Multiple tracks including Essentials of Entrepreneurship, Essentials of Finance, Leadership in the Business World, and the highly competitive M&T Summer Institute (for students interested in combining technology and business). All programs are taught by Wharton faculty using real business frameworks, case studies, and financial modeling. Students earn an official Wharton certificate upon completion. Both on-campus residential and online formats available. Acceptance is competitive.
programs.note: 2026 applications closed (standard deadline March 14). Some program tracks (Entrepreneurship, Finance, Product Design) stopped accepting new 2026 applications earlier. Apply for 2027 at globalyouth.wharton.upenn.edu — priority deadline is typically January.
